title: Main area of knowledge - code projects
description:
The biggest usage for this project is to be able to provide agents (LLMs) with concise information about code in a given project for which a knowledge graph would be created. An interface must be created so that a whole repository could be ingested and the following functions would be provided:
1) List all the files in the project
2) List all the external dependencies (libraries) used in the project
3) List all the classes in the project
4) For each class to see which classes are its dependencies (internal and external - libraries)
5) List all the types/interfaces used in the project
6) For each class to see what interface it exposes.
7) List all references using a given class
8) List all references using a given class's function
9) List all references using a given class's variable

Or any other queries/methods that make sense for an agent to ask about a code project.

As a final test for this, a test suite for THIS code project needs to be created that will show all of the above answered/solved.

features.title: Define Pydantic Models for Code Artifacts
features.description: Create a new module `src/models/code_artifact.py` to define Pydantic models for representing code structures like `CodeFile`, `ClassDefinition`, `FunctionDefinition`, and `ImportStatement`. These models will serve as the data transfer objects between the parser and the graph ingestion service.

features.title: Implement an AST-based Python Code Parser
features.description: Create a new module `src/code_parser.py`. This module will contain a `CodeParser` class that uses Python's `ast` module to parse a given Python source file. It will extract files, classes, functions, and import statements, populating the Pydantic models defined in the previous feature. This feature focuses only on parsing, not on graph interaction.

features.title: Create a Code Ingestion Service
features.description: Create a new module `src/code_ingestion_service.py`. This service will be responsible for orchestrating the analysis of a code repository. It will recursively scan a given directory for `.py` files, use the `CodeParser` to analyze each file, and then use the `GraphService` to create nodes and relationships in the knowledge graph representing the code structure (e.g., `File`, `Class` nodes and `IMPORTS`, `DEFINES` relationships) within a specified 'Area of Knowledge'.

features.title: Develop Agent Tools for Code Project Queries
features.description: Extend `src/agent_tools.py` with a new set of functions for querying the code project knowledge graph. Implement the functions listed in the story description, such as `list_files_in_project(area_name)`, `list_classes_in_project(area_name)`, `get_class_dependencies(area_name, class_name)`, etc. These functions will translate the user's question into a Cypher query and execute it against the graph via the `GraphService`.

features.title: Add API Endpoint to Trigger Code Ingestion
features.description: Create a new router in `src/routers/code_projects.py` with a POST endpoint, e.g., `/code-projects/{area_name}/ingest`. This endpoint will accept a local directory path and use the `CodeIngestionService` to start the process of analyzing the repository and populating the graph. This provides a clear entry point for the new functionality.

features.title: Create Test Suite for Self-Code-Analysis
features.description: Create a new test file @tests/scenarios/test_self_code_analysis.py . This test will perform an end-to-end validation of the new feature set by: 1. Calling the new API endpoint to ingest the project's own `src` directory. 2. Using the new functions in @src/agent_tools.py  to query the resulting graph. 3. Asserting that the queries return expected and accurate results about the project's own codebase. 4. Ensuring the test area is cleaned up afterward.

features.title: Create a javascript and typescript parser

features.title: JS/TS ingestion integration
features.description:
We have a heuristic JS/TS parser @src/js_ts_parser.py  but it is not integrated into the ingestion flow or API.
Add repository ingestion options to also scan .js/.jsx/.ts/.tsx, parse via CodeParserJSTS, and ingest comparable nodes and relationships (Files/Classes/Methods/Types, IMPORTS, CONTAINS, EXPOSES, USES_TYPE).

features.title: Richer Python ingestion (unify ingestion paths)
features.description:
There are two approaches present: @src/code_ingestion_service.py  (used by router) and @src/code_project_indexer.py  (richer ingestion producing Library/Type/Method nodes and dependencies). Consolidate into a single ingestion path with feature flags:
    - Create Library nodes for external libs from pyproject and file imports.
    - Create Type nodes and USES_TYPE relationships based on collected annotations.
    - Create Method nodes per class and EXPOSES relationships.
    - Create DEPENDS_ON_CLASS edges for class inheritance/usage where possible.

features.title: Module vs Library distinction
features.description: Current API’s list_external_dependencies returns Modules and optional Libraries, but the standard ingestion path only creates Module nodes. Ensure the ingestion pipeline can optionally create Library nodes (from pyproject or package.json) and link classes/files accordingly (DEPENDS_ON_LIB).

features.title: Method call graph and variable usage
features.description:
Current references to method/variable are best-effort (definition/exposed files). Implement call graph extraction for Python and JS/TS to support:
    - list_references_to_method: return callers (class methods/functions) and files with invocations.
    - list_references_to_class_variable: model separate Variable/Field nodes and USES/READS/WRITES edges to capture usage sites.

Internal class dependencies beyond inheritance
  - Add detection of composition/aggregation (attributes typed to other project classes) and method parameter/return types referencing other project classes to build DEPENDS_ON_CLASS edges accordingly.

features.title: API surface for code project queries
features.description:
Expose agent_tools code project functions as REST endpoints for remote use:
  - GET /code-projects/{area}/files
  - GET /code-projects/{area}/dependencies
  - GET /code-projects/{area}/classes
  - GET /code-projects/{area}/classes/{class}/dependencies
  - GET /code-projects/{area}/types
  - GET /code-projects/{area}/classes/{class}/interface
  - GET /code-projects/{area}/refs/class/{class}
  - GET /code-projects/{area}/refs/method/{class}/{method}
  - GET /code-projects/{area}/refs/variable/{class}/{variable}
Document these endpoints and wire to agent_tools or GraphService queries.

features.title: Multi-language dependency extraction
features.description:
For JS/TS, extract dependencies from import specs and optionally package.json to create Library nodes; for Python, continue to intersect imports with pyproject.toml to identify top-level libraries.
Normalize dependency names (scoped packages like @scope/name, dash/underscore normalization for Python).

features.title: Project scoping and metadata
features.description: The ingestion endpoint accepts project_id; ensure all created nodes consistently set projectId at the top level (File, Class, Module, Library, Type, Method). @src/code_ingestion_service.py  does this; verify parity when consolidating with @src/code_project_indexer.py .

features.title: Robustness, performance, and scale
features.description:
Batch Cypher operations: move repeated MERGE statements into UNWIND batches for better throughput on large codebases.

Error handling and partial retries during ingestion, with a summary report of skipped files/errors.

features.title: Tests and coverage improvements
features.description:
Add unit tests for parsers (Python and JS/TS) with edge cases (decorators, async, type annotations, generics, private members, relative imports, scoped packages, class fields syntax variations).
Add tests covering the new REST endpoints for code project queries if implemented.
Add an E2E test that ingests a mixed-language sample (Python + JS/TS) and validates cross-language dependency extraction and queries.

features.title: Documentation
features.description:
Extend README.md with a “Code Project Knowledge Graph” section covering:
  - How to run a local Neo4j test instance and seed (link to tests/neo4j docs).
  - How to ingest a repository (Python and JS/TS only today; future: multi-language) and run agent queries.
  - Data model conventions: labels (Area, File, Class, Method, Module, Library, Type), relationship types (BELONGS_TO, DEFINES, CONTAINS, IMPORTS, EXPOSES, USES_TYPE, DEPENDS_ON_CLASS, DEPENDS_ON_LIB).

features.title: Operational concerns
features.description:
Provide containerized Neo4j for local dev via docker-compose with default creds matching tests (already present under tests/neo4j).Add make targets to start API + DB.
Add observability: structured logging around ingestion phases and counts, optional metrics.

features.title: Prepare a showcase as to how to use this project
features.description:
The use case is the following:
There's the package 'graphiti-core' (this project uses it so it can be used as reference) - an external project wants to learn about it and use it appropriately. A guide in @docs/FIRST_STEPS.md  should be written - detailing the process of an external process supplying all the code for 'graphiti-core' and getting all the relevant information. So it should be very easy to setup a graph for such a package and as a result retrieve some sort of root node that will serve as a summary. From then on anyone can query about this package and retrieve appropriate information.

features.title: Look at the project and cleanup any dead or duplicate code
features.description:
Make the whole repository cleaner and work well together.
It should be easily extensible for future language parsers or domain specific areas/blueprints etc.

features.title: Follow the official graphiti guide
features.description:
Looking here:
https://help.getzep.com/graphiti/core-concepts/custom-entity-and-edge-types

It follows that all EntityNodes must be flat - i.e. shouldn't have any dictionaries as fields. The `create_node` in @src/graph_service.py must be updated to flatten the attributes directly onto the node so only primitives and arrays are stored as fields.

features.title: Use the official guides to make this project better
features.description:
Looking at here:
https://help.getzep.com/graphiti/core-concepts/graph-namespacing
and
https://help.getzep.com/graphiti/core-concepts/communities
and especially:
https://help.getzep.com/graphiti/working-with-data/searching

We are missing some core functionality that is exposed by graphiti.
Go over these resources and create a document @docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md that will highlight step by step features that we should add to make this project better.

features.title: Follow the official guide to strongly type
features.description:
Looking here:
https://help.getzep.com/graphiti/core-concepts/custom-entity-and-edge-types

It follows that all EntityNodes must be strongly type by extending BaseModel just like it's shown in the guide and just like we do already in @src/models/blueprint.py  . This means that all code related EntityNodes that are used in @src/agent_tools.py  for instance, would have to have their model (which would be great anyway to have them strongly typed).
All queries must be updated to match the new models.
This is also one of the reasons why @tests/scenarios/test_self_code_analysis.py  doesn't work, because we cannot have queries such as `c.attributes.class_name = $cls` .
